summary:
Visitors to Nord-Est stand under the national framework of Italy. Entry rules, identity documents, legal gender recognition, criminal law and the national protection and health-care layers are set by Italy and are recorded in the country's own dossier. The material identified at region level concerns Veneto and, in narrower form, Emilia-Romagna.

The Veneto Regional Council passed motion n.340 at its 178th public session in Venice on 3 July. Deliberation n.92 of 14 October 2014 approved that motion, committing the regional government to a mandatory 'Natural Family Day' observance on the last school day before Christmas and rejecting the aims of gender-awareness content in schools. The official regional government bulletin carries the primary-source text of the deliberation. The most recent documented instance of this instrument in this record is 14 October 2014; no later amendment, repeal or successor measure is documented here.

The Veneto measure operates through the school calendar and regional policy statements. It creates no criminal offence, no penalty and no restriction on entry, documents or movement, and it does not alter the national rules on legal gender recognition or anti-discrimination protection.
tangentialFactors:
Regional anti-discrimination statutes in the parent framework cover Emilia-Romagna (2019) alongside eight other Italian regions, giving one part of Nord-Est a region-level discrimination statute while Veneto's documented regional instrument runs in the opposite direction, committing the regional government to a mandatory 'Natural Family Day' school observance and to rejecting gender-awareness content. Friuli-Venezia Giulia and Trentino-Alto Adige have no regional statute listed in this inventory.

The Veneto deliberation is a policy and school-observance instrument rather than an enforcement power; comparisons with criminal law or border measures are not apt, since those sit entirely at national level.
localsOnly:
For residents of Veneto, deliberation n.92 of 14 October 2014 binds the regional government to hold the 'Natural Family Day' observance on the last school day before Christmas, and records the regional council's rejection of the aims of gender-awareness content. The obligation falls on the regional administration and the school system, not on individuals.

Residents of Emilia-Romagna are covered by that region's 2019 anti-discrimination statute, which is a regional instrument distinct from Italy's national employment-discrimination rules.
outOfScopeNotes:
No region-specific detention findings for facilities in Nord-Est are sourced here. The national detention material in this inventory, including the July 2025 Ludwig Boltzmann Institute report and the 2026 Frontiers in Psychiatry analysis of trans prisoners, is not broken down by region, and the documented prison cases (Pozzale near Florence, Rebibbia in Rome, Poggioreale in Naples, Terni, Sollicciano in Florence) all sit outside Nord-Est. Whether trans detainees in Nord-Est facilities face the same placement and hormone-access problems described nationally is unresolved in this record.

No region-specific incidents of violence against transgender people in Nord-Est are documented in this inventory, and no region-level survey of trans residents' experiences in Nord-Est is sourced. The absence of such material is not evidence of their absence.

Whether motion n.340 or deliberation n.92 has been implemented, funded or observed in practice since 14 October 2014 is not sourced here.
